title: Remove personal contact info / ID numbers via 'Results about you'
whenItApplies: A Google Search result shows the subject's own phone number, home address, email address, or (where supported) SSN, passport number or driver's license number. Feature rolling out to users over 18 in certain markets.
notEligible: Info the subject controls themselves (own social profile/blog); results from pages Google deems valuable to the public (educational or government institutions, newspapers); professional info (use the detailed removal form if posted with intent to harm); requests for someone else filed from your own account may be denied.
evidence: Name and the exact contact info as it appears on the result (e.g. nickname or old address as shown)
The result URL(s)
Signed-in Google Account (status updates go to its email)
steps: Open Results about you (Google app: profile menu > Results about you; web: myactivity.google.com/results-about-you) and select Get started/Settings
Enter name and personal contact info to monitor; optionally enable email/app notifications
Review matches in the 'To review' tab; select a result > Request to remove
Alternatively from a Search result: More (three dots) > Remove result > It shows my personal info > Contact info, complete the flow
Track status (In progress / Approved / Denied / Undone) under 'Removal requests'
If denied, read the stated reason; if the source site owner removes the data, use the Refresh Outdated Content tool
timeline: Notifications of matches and the submission confirmation email arrive 'within a few hours'; Google notes a possible delay between approval and the result disappearing. No overall review SLA stated.

title: Remove private PII and doxxing content (detailed removal request form)
whenItApplies: Result URL shows the subject's confidential PII: government ID numbers (SSN, tax ID, resident ID), bank/credit card numbers, images of signature or ID, private records such as medical records, confidential usernames/passwords, address/phone/email; OR doxxing: personal info with explicit/implicit threats or calls to harass, or a significant amount of aggregated personal info without legitimate purpose.
notEligible: Content that is newsworthy / of public interest may be kept. Google only removes from Search results, not from the host site.
evidence: Exact URL(s) of each page containing the info (only listed URLs are reviewed)
Screenshots showing the info (may be cropped)
For doxxing: evidence of threats/calls to harm, or of aggregation
steps: Collect each page URL and screenshots
Open the content removal form and select the personal-info/doxxing path
Enter the subject's details and the URLs; upload screenshots
Submit; watch for Google's email decision
Outcome may be full removal or query-based removal (hidden only for queries containing the subject's name)
Separately ask the website owner to delete the content at source
letterOutline: Subject identification and relationship of submitter (self or representative)
Policy invoked: personally identifiable information / doxxing
List of URLs with the exact PII shown on each
Why it is confidential or how it is used to threaten/harass
Request for removal from Google Search results

title: Refresh Outdated Content tool (page/image removed or changed at source)
whenItApplies: You do not own the page, and the page or image no longer exists or the sensitive content has been significantly changed/removed, but Google still shows the old snippet or cached result.
notEligible: Content still live on the page; info you think is wrong/harmful but still present; you are a verified Search Console owner (use the Removals tool instead); you just want a recrawl; you want permanent removal of a live URL.
evidence: Exact result URL (right-click > Copy link address from Google results)
For images: image URL plus containing page URL (separate request per page)
If page still exists: 1-2 words from the old snippet that no longer appear live
steps: Confirm the content has been removed or changed at source
Sign in with a Google Account and open the Refresh Outdated Content tool
Select New request (Page or Image) and paste the URL in the required format
Submit; supply removed snippet words if prompted
Check status in the request queue (Pending/Approved/Denied/Expired/Cancelled)
Submit separate requests for every duplicate URL variant still appearing
timeline: Pending processing 'can take a few days'. Approved requests expire after 180 days or when the URL no longer exists.

whenItApplies: Content believed to violate the law or the requester's rights (e.g. defamation, court orders, trademark, other local-law claims) that is not covered by Google's personal-content policies.

Specific statements/content that is unlawful and why

timeline: Google states it endeavours to respond 'as soon as we can'; no fixed timeline.

Why statements are false/unlawful and the harm caused

title: Elements of a valid DMCA takedown notice (17 U.S.C. § 512(c)(3)(A))
whenItApplies: Copyrighted material hosted by a service provider without authorization; notice goes to the provider's designated agent.
notEligible: Non-copyright claims (defamation, privacy, names) are not DMCA matters; Google reports rejecting such abusive notices. Knowing material misrepresentation creates liability under § 512(f).
contact: The service provider's DMCA designated agent (see Copyright Office directory)
evidence: (i) Physical or electronic signature of a person authorized to act for the owner
(ii) Identification of the copyrighted work (or representative list for multiple works on one site)
(iii) Identification of the infringing material and information reasonably sufficient to locate it
(iv) Complainant contact info: address, telephone, and email if available
(v) Statement of good-faith belief that use is not authorized by owner, agent, or law
(vi) Statement that the notice is accurate and, under penalty of perjury, that complainant is authorized to act for the owner
steps: Confirm ownership/authority and consider fair use
Locate the host and its designated agent
Draft notice with all six elements
Send to the designated agent (or provider webform)
If a counter-notice is received, provider restores material in 10-14 business days unless you notify it that you filed a court action
timeline: Statute requires providers to respond 'expeditiously'; counter-notice restoration window is not less than 10 nor more than 14 business days after receipt (§ 512(g)(2)(C)).
letterOutline: Header: DMCA Notice of Claimed Infringement, addressed to designated agent
Accuracy and authority statement under penalty of perjury

whenItApplies: Content about the subject on Justia.
notes: UNVERIFIED: official pages bot-challenged or unreachable via egress exits. No policy facts recorded.

title: Facebook defamation report form
whenItApplies: Content on Facebook believed defamatory.
notEligible: Facebook states it is not in a position to adjudicate truth and, consistent with CDA 230(c), generally cannot act without a court order establishing unlawfulness (US).
evidence: URL for each piece of content
Specific statements alleged defamatory and why
Country where legal rights claimed
Court order where required
steps: Select type of unlawfulness and country
State on whose behalf you report (self, organization, attorney/representative)
Provide URLs and explanation per item
Contact the poster; obtain a court order if needed
letterOutline: Reporter identity and authority (injured person or authorized representative)

title: Facebook privacy violation (photo/video) report
whenItApplies: Photo or video on Facebook believed to violate the subject's privacy; private info that could lead to physical/financial harm (Meta Privacy Violations policy).
notEligible: Meta may allow private info that became public through news, court filings, press releases.
steps: Remove/report unwanted tags
Use the privacy violation form linked from 'Reporting a Privacy Violation'
Parents of children under 13 / representatives of incapacitated persons use the privacy contact form (facebook.com/help/contact/516343134409068)
notes: Privacy form ID extracted from the help article markup; form page itself not separately fetched.

title: Instagram exposed private information report
whenItApplies: Photo/video or post exposing the reporter's private/confidential information on Instagram.
notEligible: Instagram cannot remove info posted publicly elsewhere; acts only if associated with the reporter or with documentation of authority.
steps: Optionally ask the poster to remove it
Report via the privacy form; reports are anonymous except IP reports

title: Meta Bullying & Harassment policy
whenItApplies: Targeted harassment; private adults must self-report for some protections.
steps: Report in-app; self-report where the policy requires it
notes: Facebook/Instagram review (Recommendations) reporting flow not verified.

title: Reddit personal information violation
whenItApplies: Posting someone's personal information or links to it (incl. legible Facebook screenshots). Public-figure professional contact info may be an exception.
steps: Report via reddit.com/report (Personal Information)
Contact Reddit support if unresolved

title: X private information & media policy
whenItApplies: Posting/threatening to expose home address/location, ID documents, non-public contact info, identity of an anonymous user; private media of individuals shared without consent.
notEligible: Publicly available info shared non-abusively; business locations; media of public interest/newsworthy.
evidence: Post URLs
Private media: first-person report (or authorized/legal representative)
steps: Report via the private information form or in-app
Anyone may report clearly abusive sharing; otherwise X may need the owner or authorized representative

title: X abuse/harassment and copyright (DMCA) reports
whenItApplies: Abusive behavior/harassment; or copyright infringement (profile/header images, media, posts).
steps: Harassment: report via abuse form; X may need to hear from the target
Copyright: Intellectual Property form > report copyright infringement (DMCA), counter-notice and retraction options available

title: TikTok privacy, harassment and copyright reports
whenItApplies: Harassment/bullying incl. doxing; sharing personal information that could lead to harm (identity theft, stalking, fraud); copyright infringement.
notEligible: More critical commentary allowed about public figures.
steps: Report in-app or via 'Report a problem' > Report a potential violation
Privacy: tiktok.com/legal/report/privacy
Copyright: Copyright Infringement Report online form (ipr.tiktokforbusiness.com/legal/report/Copyright) with option to prevent re-uploads

title: Paid-contribution disclosure (Wikimedia Terms of Use + WP:PAID)
whenItApplies: Anyone editing for compensation (incl. reputation agencies and their clients).
notEligible: Undisclosed paid editing violates the Terms of Use; violators agree to binding 'Med-Arb'.
evidence: Disclosure of employer, client, and affiliation
steps: Disclose employer, client, intended beneficiary and affiliation on user page, talk page, or edit summary of each paid contribution (en.wiki: {{paid|employer=...|client=...}} / {{connected contributor (paid)}})
Link from user page to all accounts on sites where paid editing is advertised/solicited
Link to Wikipedia account(s) in off-wiki ads and in communications with each client
Do not log out to edit

title: Conflict of interest guideline (WP:COI)
whenItApplies: Subject, employee, agent or anyone with a COI regarding an article.
notEligible: COI editors are strongly discouraged from editing affected articles directly; must not act as AfC/NPP reviewer of affected articles; no one controls articles.
steps: Disclose COI
Propose changes on the article talk page with {{edit COI}}
Put new articles through Articles for Creation
Keep discussions concise; editors may decline requests
See Guide to effective COI edit requests

title: Edit request for article subjects (talk page / {{edit COI}})
whenItApplies: Subject or representative wants factual corrections or additions.
evidence: Reliable, published, independent sources supporting each change
steps: Open the article's Talk page > New section
State exact change requested ('change X to Y'), with citations
Add {{edit COI}} (COI/paid) to queue it; optionally use the Edit Request Wizard
Wait for a volunteer; requests may be declined

title: Biographies of living persons (WP:BLP) issues
whenItApplies: Unsourced or poorly sourced contentious material about a living person.
notEligible: Editors in a significant dispute with the subject should not edit their biography.
contact: info-en-q@wikimedia.org (Volunteer Response Team, for legal or serious concerns; include article link and details)
steps: Cite WP:BLP: contentious unsourced/poorly sourced material should be removed immediately
Raise on article talk page or BLP Noticeboard
For serious/legal concerns email VRT

title: Articles for Creation (AfC)
whenItApplies: New article drafts, required route for COI/paid editors; new or unregistered editors who cannot create mainspace articles.
steps: Create draft via Article Wizard
Focus on references establishing notability
Submit for review; volunteers review
timeline: No fixed waiting time; not reviewed in submission order.

title: Notability tests (WP:GNG, WP:BIO, WP:CORP/NCORP)
whenItApplies: Before drafting or defending an article.
notEligible: Trivial/incidental coverage, press releases, company sites, routine announcements do not establish notability; organizations not notable via association.
steps: GNG: significant coverage in reliable sources independent of the subject
BIO: significant coverage in multiple published, reliable, intellectually independent secondary sources
CORP: each source must contain significant, in-depth coverage, be completely independent, reliable, and secondary
